answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil attacks are resisted by binding each agent to a unique hardware attestation that creates a continuous marble of verifiable compute history. These are mapped into a shared atlas of trusted peers, while new or low-reputation agents are temporarily placed on an isolation island for observation. The attacker must acquire and maintain distinct physical devices for every fake identity, imposing high hardware and energy costs that scale linearly with the number of sybils.
